collections.name: Credits in Motion
collections.description:
Credits in Motion is an independent animated pixel-art experiment inspired by the visual language of Jack Butcher’s Credits.
10,000 unique compositions. Each artwork is constructed pixel by pixel — individual blocks appear in sequence, gradually assembling into the final piece before the cycle begins again.
Every composition and assembly sequence is unique.
But this collection is about more than movement.
50% of mint proceeds and 50% of creator fees are dedicated to supporting children through Adam Weitsman and Make-A-Wish.
This continues a charitable initiative I previously started with DROUPZ, a collection created by me. Through DROUPZ, donations from the project were directed to Make-A-Wish through Adam Weitsman.
With Credits in Motion, that idea continues:
Pixels move. Kindness continues.
Independent project. Inspired by Credits. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Jack Butcher or the original Credits collection.

collections.name: Midnight Miners
collections.description:
10,000 machines. One workshop that never sleeps.

Beyond the last neon sign, behind a door nobody remembers opening, the workshop is still running.

Fans hum. Cables snake across crowded benches. An amber screen flickers in the dark. Then another. These machines were supposed to be obsolete. Apparently, nobody told them.

Midnight Miners is a collection built around 10,000 collectible computer characters and a world where old hardware has a personality of its own. Inspired by retro CRT monitors, custom computer builds and the atmosphere of late-night workshops, it turns familiar technology into characters worth getting attached to.

The visual world brings together expressive screens, chunky cases, cooling fans and warm lights against deep midnight blues. Some machines look ready for another shift. Others look like they have already worked a thousand. Together, they belong to the same place

Find your machine. Keep the night running.

collections.name: Reliquia: LEGACY
collections.description:
3,333 relics, drawn and stored entirely onchain. No IPFS, no server, no image
files — every pixel is generated by contract code on Robinhood Chain.

A relic does not arrive finished. It mints as a scatter of bone and gathers
itself over five days, one percent roughly every seventy minutes, until it
stands whole. The clock starts at your mint and belongs to your token: it never
resets when a relic changes hands. Buy one mid-formation and it carries on from
exactly where it was.

There is no reveal. A relic is entirely itself from the block it mints in —
its species, its damage, its colour — and formation only says how much of it has
arrived so far.

No two are the same colour. Each of the 3,333 carries its own bone palette and
its own background, stored as contract code rather than chosen from a list, so
there is no shared skin and no repeated ground anywhere in the collection.

Ten are 1/1 They hold ids 1 through 10, reserved before the mint
opened, and publish nothing but a name.

collections.name: Mining Systems
collections.description:
Start a new chapter.

Mining Systems is a collection of 3,500 animated pixel-art NFTs built around one core idea: your equipment becomes the starting point of an expanding mining journey.

AFTER THE MINT

The project will allow holders to activate eligible systems, automatically farm points, and upgrade their equipment. Offline progress will accumulate for up to 24 hours.

FROM POINTS TO TOKENS

The economic model allocates 12,000,000 tokens to players from a total supply of 20,170,000 tokens.

Each player's allocation will depend on the number of points they earn relative to the total points generated by the community.

Spending points on upgrades will not reduce the final score used to calculate token allocation.

Final mining rates, activation requirements, and distribution rules will be published before launch.

Build your system. Upgrade your equipment. Stay tuned for what comes next.

collections.name: Clay StonKz
collections.description:
Clay StonKz is a collection of 6,969 clay characters inspired by markets, memes, crypto, stocks, bulls, bears, wins, losses, and the occasional rug pullz.

Every character and trait begins in the physical world. Brrrbon sculpt the clay by hand, photograph it, then bring those images into the digital world where they’re layered together to create the final collection.

Fingerprints, dents, uneven edges, mistakes, and texture are all part of the work. I’m not trying to make clay look digital. I’m trying to make the digital world look like it was made out of clay.

Real clay. Real photography.
Created physically. Collected digitally.

collections.name: ALTERHOOD
collections.description: ALTERHOOD is a lore-driven PFP collection set in a sealed world where humanity survived, but not unchanged. Beneath the surface, generations adapted to an environment that could no longer be repaired. The Vault was built as a last attempt to preserve life, but eventually became a city, a laboratory, a nursery and an emergency state. At its center is MOTHER, the intelligence created to coordinate everything required for life to continue. When preservation was no longer enough, MOTHER chose adaptation. ALTERHOOD consists of 10,000 unique characters across 40 distinct Origins, with 250 characters per Origin. Each Origin represents a different response to survival, shaped by its own biology, culture, identity and visual language. Built on Robinhood Chain, ALTERHOOD is the first entry into a larger world designed to expand through lore, characters, stories, collaborations and future experiences. Humanity survived. But not as it remembered itself.

collections.name: Facets
collections.description:
FACETS is an art collection of 2,222 pieces built on seven distinct personas from the web3 space, each with its own story and characteristics. Fully on-chain and animated, drawn in Solidity as pixel blocks on a 35x35 grid.

It carries two mechanics: Burn to Forge, and The Turn, which shares royalties with holders. Every piece also turns toward the wallet holding it and is redrawn when it changes hands, and each one carries a name from a book of 832, written by hand.
